decision.title: Phase 6 plan: one host shim under JavaScript, Kotlin and Swift (packet )
decision.summary: Phase 6 moves the JavaScript shim to bindings/host/ as one that JavaScript, Kotlin (through JNI glue) and Swift (through a module map) all link, with no public header change.

body.p: , after , , , , , , , . Plans Phase 6 (PLAN.md) in docs/tasks/phase-6.md, as and planned Phases 5 and 7.

item.p: Mechanism: the JavaScript shim already turns the public API into handles, flat requests, one error per processor, side results () and JSON-shaped input. Packet moves it to bindings/host/ as the host shim (glossary ). The resolver becomes an interface (state and function) instead of a WebAssembly import.
JavaScript links it with a thin export file. The export names, and so src/index.ts, do not change.
Kotlin adds only a JNI glue file.
Swift imports the shim through a module map and adds no C.
A second or third C adapter would duplicate value conversion, side results and error copying. No public header changes.
APIs (in the task file): the JavaScript package's concepts with each language's idiom.

Shared concepts: Processor (resolver, features, collation data), parse, compile once and evaluate many times, value by the fn:parse-json rule, serialize with fn:serialize's options, compileQuery, compileStylesheet, compileSchema, side results after the call, errors with status, code, source name, line and column.
Each language's idiom: named arguments with defaults instead of option objects.
There is no load(): a native library is not fetched.
Ownership:
Kotlin: objects are AutoCloseable with a Cleaner backstop. Objects hold their processor strongly, and closing a processor closes what it made. Every call holds the processor's lock ().
Swift: ARC; objects retain their processor. They are not Sendable, and Swift 6 strict concurrency enforces at compile time.

Callbacks: the resolver alone runs during a call and must not use its processor (). The binding keeps an exception it throws and rethrows it after the shim fails with INPUT_OUTPUT_FAILED, so the JNI glue never handles a pending JVM exception.

JNI rules: every native is (JNIEnv *, jclass, jobject request), three parameters (glossary ). Field IDs are cached per processor, not in globals. Text is UTF-8 ByteArray, never jstring, because JNI's modified UTF-8 differs for U+0000 and supplementary characters.
Libraries: one per platform, each with every language and every feature except EXPath File:
libsxml_kotlin.so for Android and the JVM, exporting the JNI symbols only;
Sxml.xcframework (static) for iOS and macOS;
the CMake target sxml_host for Swift on Linux.
A core-only native variant waits for a host that asks for it.
Probe here (2026-10-20, Linux x86_64, no KVM, no macOS):

NDK r28c builds the library with -Werror for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64 and x86 at API 29. At API 24 and 28, only aligned_alloc (src/allocator.c, bionic API 28) and timespec_get (src/processor.c, API 29) are missing. 6.3 adds one __ANDROID_API__ branch for each, and minSdk is 24 ( default).
Kotlin 2.2.20 with JNI on JDK 21 runs the shim and calls back into a lambda.
Gradle 8.14.3 with AGP 8.10.1 assembles an AAR with the four ABIs (Maven Central answers 429 at times: retry).
Swift 6.2 on Linux runs the shim through a module map.
No emulator (no /dev/kvm). iOS needs the owner's macOS.

Pins: NDK r28c (16 KB pages), platform 35, minSdk 24, Kotlin 2.2.20, JDK 21, Gradle 8.14.3, AGP 8.10.1, Swift 6.2, iOS 15, macOS 13. tools/fetch-binding-toolchains.sh (6.3) fetches them into a scratchpad directory.
Packets:
6.2: host shim;
6.3: Android build and fallbacks;
6.4, 6.5: Kotlin;
6.9: Apple builds (owner);
6.10: device CI (written here, disabled until the owner enables it, );
6.11: documentation and release steps;
6.12: review.
6.2 to 6.8 and 6.11 run here. Device runs, 6.9 and publishing are the owner's.
Tests: parity by name with test/package.test.ts and test/full.test.ts, 0 leaks, the allocation-failure loop (). The ctests are:
kotlin/jvm: kotlinc and kotlin.test, with no Gradle or network under ctest;
swift/linux;
android/build.
On devices: Android instrumented tests on an emulator at API 24 and 35 and one arm64 device; xcodebuild test on an iOS simulator and device.
Defaults taken (; outward-facing, so the owner may change them before a release):
Kotlin package dev.tinyactors.sxml, Maven coordinates dev.tinyactors:sxml-android and :sxml-jvm ();
Swift module Sxml, with Package.swift at the repository root;
size budget for libsxml_kotlin.so on arm64-v8a: 9,000,000 stripped, 2,400,000 gzipped.
Gate (proposed):
the parity list passes on the JVM and Linux Swift;
the four ABIs build at API 24, and the AAR is within its budget;
instrumented tests pass on the emulator and an arm64 device;
Swift passes on macOS, an iOS simulator and a device;
the bindings workflow is green once CI is on;
the JavaScript tests and sizes are unchanged, and no conformance count has dropped.
PLAN.md: the Phase 6 row names the host shim and the device gate.
